title: Peregrine edge-scale benchmark: latency, throughput, cost scenarios
content:
Executive summary:

This report captures the results of a two-week performance sweep for the Peregrine fintech POC (edge-scale deployment). Objectives were to understand tail latency behavior under bursty traffic, quantify throughput per-node across quantization and batch configs, model token-level cost at different concurrency profiles, and validate cache and cold-start strategies for a private edge footprint. Testing focused on a representative LLM serving workload: multi-turn chat + short-document extraction (avg 120 tokens request, 200 token response).

Key findings (high level):
- Warm-cache single-GPU p95 latency: 78–110 ms depending on batch and quantization (q4_0 fastest).
- Cold-start median latency penalty: +230–550 ms on first request for new KV contexts (depends on model size and tokenizer warmup).
- Throughput per 80GB A100-equivalent node: sustained 175–420 requests/minute across configs (higher for q4_0 with batching).
- Cost per 1M output tokens (server-side compute only): $38 (baseline fp16, no batching) down to $9 (q4_0 + batching + caching).
- Best operational tradeoff for Peregrine: q4_0 quantization + small batching (batch size 4) + aggressive prefix KV caching yields ~2.5x cost reduction with <15% p95 latency regression in steady-state.

Testbed and methodology:
- Infrastructure: 3-node private cluster simulating edge sites (node spec: 80GB GPU, 512GB RAM, NVMe; network: 10Gbps; control-plane outside cluster).
- Models: open-llm-family/peregrine-13b-v1 (fp16), same model converted to q4_0 and q8_0 variants.
- Workloads: three synthetic profiles derived from Peregrine telemetry: (A) chat-heavy (70% small replies), (B) doc-extract (20% long summaries), (C) microburst (spike: 300 concurrent ephemeral short requests).
- Measurement windows: cold-start (empty KV, first request), warm (steady-state after 30s of steady traffic), and recovery (post-microburst SLO recovery time).
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies end-to-end, tail token generation time, server GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, request queuing time, throughput, and estimated server compute cost (based on reserved capacity pricing model).

Detailed results (selected):
- Chat-heavy profile, q4_0, batch=4: p50=42ms, p95=98ms, p99=210ms, throughput=390 req/min, GPU util=72%, kv-cache-hit=68%. Cost est = $11/1M tokens.
- Doc-extract, fp16, batch=1: p50=125ms, p95=320ms, p99=780ms, throughput=175 req/min, gpu util=38%, kv-cache-hit ~12%. Cost est = $38/1M tokens.
- Microburst profile, q8_0, batch auto: observed queue spikes leading to p95 > 800ms and transient OOMs on memory-heavy tails when multiple long requests coincided. Recovery time to baseline p95 averaged 18s after spike subsided when autoscaling was enabled with 2s ramp.

Operational observations and runbook items:
- Cold-start mitigation: pre-warm KV cache for active sessions during known release windows; use light-weight ephemeral pooling to eliminate first-token stalls for critical routes.
- Batching policy: prefer small bounded batching (2–4) for low-latency chat routes; larger batches (8–16) beneficial for batch-offline jobs but hurt tail latency for interactive flows.
- Quantization caveats: q4_0 gives best cost/throughput but increases p99 variance on long-context requests; recommend canarying q4_0 on non-critical routes and using fp16 fallback for long-document mode.
- Autoscaling policy: configured cooldown too low in initial tests (30s) causing oscillation; bump to 90s and use request queues + backpressure indicators (queued requests > 200) to trigger scale-up.

Cost model notes:
- Server compute only; excludes networking and control-plane overhead.
- Base assumptions: node hourly cost equivalent to our private-reserved SKU priced at $3.50/hr (internal equivalent) and amortized across measured throughput.
- Example: under chat-heavy q4_0 batch=4 config, measured throughput ~390 rpm -> 6.5 rps. With average tokens per response ~200, token throughput ~1300 tps. Using per-node throughput we estimate $9–12 per 1M output tokens.

Recommendations for Peregrine POC next phase:
1) Adopt q4_0 on non-sensitive chat routes with fp16 fallback for long-document extraction.
2) Implement a two-tier routing policy: low-latency chat routes pinned to small batching + pre-warmed KV; batch/analytics routes run on higher-batch nodes.
3) Add a <30s warm pool of GPUs for predictable traffic spikes (microburst protection), and tune autoscale cooldown to 90s.
4) Instrument per-route token accounting and surface cost-neutrality alerts in Console (threshold 20% cost drift).
5) Run a longer 72-hour soak test with production traces to validate p99 stability under mixed traffic.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Quantize-and-finetune tradeoff: can we retrain a q4_0 variant to narrow the p99 gap for long-context docs? (Research task, assigned to Applied ML)
- Network impact: need to re-run microburst tests with WAN emulation (higher latencies) to validate edge-region behavior.
- SLA modeling: map these results to potential commercial SLAs (p95 < 150ms for chat) and pricing tiers.
